points.title: What breaks 1NF
points.must: A field with several values in one cell or repeating columns (Phone1, Phone2…), with an example such as Country = “Kazakhstan, France”.

points.title: Converting to 1NF
points.must: Make values atomic (one row per value / split fields), remove repeating groups, choose a primary key — often composite.

points.title: 1NF example
points.must: Movies table rewritten with one row per film–country pair and key (MovieID, Country).

points.title: Checking for 2NF
points.must: If the key is a single field the table is already 2NF; if composite, check whether each field depends on the whole key.

points.title: Converting to 2NF
points.must: Move fields that depend on part of the key into a new table with that part as its primary key; keep it in the original table as a foreign key.

points.title: 2NF example
points.must: Movies(MovieID, Title, Year) and MovieCountries(MovieID*, Country), or OrderLines / Products.

points.title: Transitive dependency
points.must: A non-key field depends on another non-key field, with an example (CourseID → TeacherName → TeacherDateOfBirth).

points.title: Converting to 3NF
points.must: Move the dependent fields to a new table; the field they depend on becomes its primary key and stays as a foreign key in the original table.

points.title: 3NF example
points.must: Teachers(TeacherID, TeacherName, DateOfBirth) and Courses(CourseID, CourseName, TeacherID*), linked 1:M.

points.title: Notation
points.must: Primary keys underlined, foreign keys marked with *; table written as TableName(Field1, Field2, …).

points.title: What each step removes
points.must: Table or list: 1NF lists/repeating groups, 2NF partial dependencies, 3NF transitive dependencies, and the key of each new table.

points.title: Common mistakes
points.must: Forgetting the foreign key, losing a field, using a name as a key, confusing partial and transitive dependencies.
